blocks.note: first meaning: someone who raises a glass in honour of another
second meaning: the kitchen gadget that browns bread

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like a robot butler that salutes; split it, and each half is a separate meaning of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Proposing a toast is a way of honouring someone, and the kitchen machine that crisps sliced bread carries the same name.

clue.text: Heads of trade and industry caught hiding illegal practice from China

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.clueFragment: trade and industry caught hiding illegal
blocks.note: the leading letters of six consecutive words

explanation.surface: Business leaders have been caught concealing some unlawful dealing linked to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of trade and industry' looks like business chiefs, but the heads run on through 'caught hiding illegal' too: six initials in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a slow martial-arts exercise routine that originated in China and is practised daily by many people.

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey
the flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a donkey along with an annoying bird, 'flipping' used as a mild curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, as in 'that flipping bird', but it turns the bird round.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a role or a name is to take it on as your own, the same sense as adopting it.

clue.text: Equivalent sum found by worker after time

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a worker ant; ants are crossword workers
a sum of money is an amount

explanation.surface: An accountant finds a matching total after hours of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces back to front: the worker follows time, and the sum sits beside that pair at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount means equal in value or effect, used in phrases like 'tantamount to theft'.

clue.text: Food store upset after second bit of produce is put out

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something tips it over so it reads bottom to top
the second bit of a word is its second letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the second letter of the word
a deli is a shop selling prepared foods

explanation.surface: A grocer's stock is ruined after some produce is thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' feels like discarding the produce, but the definition is the whole phrase 'is put out', meaning annoyed; the overturned shop follows the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled is a past participle meaning irritated, so 'is riled' and 'is put out' both say someone is annoyed.

blocks.note: 'up' can mean worked up or excited
in maths a radical is a root, as in the square-root sign

explanation.surface: Fired-up political extremists push people out of their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radicals' looks like a political word, but it is the mathematical sense: a radical sign marks a root.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot people is to force them from their home or settled place, which is what displacing them means.

indicators.note: engineering is constructing or contriving, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Engineering lecturers gathered for some drastic meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineering tutors' reads as the subject they teach; 'engineering' is actually the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttermost means furthest or greatest in degree, an old-fashioned synonym of utmost.

indicators.note: with no heart, the central letter of the word is taken away

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Phone calls from uncaring medics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like the noun for physicians, but it is the verb: to doctor results is to tamper with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig an election or a game is to fix it dishonestly, the same as doctoring the figures.

blocks.note: to out someone is to reveal their secret
a short holiday is a break

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a skin rash picked up on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' tempts as the adjective for reckless; here it is the noun, a sudden eruption on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of spots is a rash, and more widely a sudden eruption of something unwelcome.

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
trimmer means tidier or neater

explanation.surface: A boy owns a tidier lawn-mowing tool than his father.
explanation.walkthrough: A Strimmer is the British brand name, now used generally, for a nylon-line grass trimmer, called a weed whacker in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a hand-held power tool with a spinning line that slices through long weeds and lawn edges.

clue.text: Playwright messed up bins having taken drug

indicators.note: something messed up is jumbled out of its proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A dramatist on drugs knocks over the rubbish bins.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug is added to the bins before they are rearranged, so all five letters go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist behind A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Rig total I revised for one arguing in court

indicators.note: a revised version is altered and reworked, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles a figure and changes the total in a legal dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rig' sounds like the crooked act at the heart of a trial, but it is simply letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigator is a lawyer who specialises in conducting lawsuits and presenting cases before judges.

clue.text: Safe house Andrew keeps doctor in

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: a house is a home
Andy is the short form of Andrew
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Andrew keeps a doctor living at his safe house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe house' looks like one unit, a hideout, but 'Safe' alone is the definition and 'house' starts the wordplay; the final 'in' just ends the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Home and dry is a British idiom meaning secure and successful, with all danger or difficulty behind you.

blocks.note: first meaning: odd or peculiar, in old-fashioned British slang
second meaning: the spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'a rum do' or 'a rum fellow' means something strange, which is the less familiar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is dated slang for odd or queer, and also the name of the liquor made from molasses.

blocks.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
a ration is a fixed allowance, a budget

explanation.surface: Keeping to a budget is a sign of personal restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single moral about thrift; it is just two synonyms placed end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderation is avoiding excess, keeping your behaviour within reasonable limits by your own choice.

clue.text: Colonel overcome by awful toothache gets soothing drink

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters are knocked out of order
to be overcome by something is to be swamped by it, so one piece is engulfed by the other

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written
Col is the military abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: An officer laid low by dreadful toothache is given a comforting warm drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged toothache letters wrap around the officer's abbreviation, which sits just after the first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate is a warm milky cocoa beverage, traditionally sipped for comfort or before bed.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: So much alarm has distressed the monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like it describes the monkeys' mood, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Capuchins are small, clever South American primates, named after the hooded friars whose habits their markings resemble.

clue.text: Deer encountering initially noisy insect is motionless

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer
the first letter
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A deer meeting a buzzing insect freezes on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'noisy insect' one creature, but 'initially' takes only the first letter of 'noisy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant describes water or air that does not flow, still and unmoving, and so is a synonym of motionless.

blocks.note: far means distant
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Something spotted far away turns out to be an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was a pre-1971 British coin worth a quarter of an old penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was a small bronze coin of British currency, withdrawn in 1960, so it is a former piece of money.

blocks.note: to train someone is to teach them
a potter makes ceramics

explanation.surface: A pottery teacher who is something of a geek.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a trainspotter is a hobbyist who logs locomotive numbers, and the word is shorthand for an obsessive anorak.
explanation.definitionFit: Train spotters are the stock British image of an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, so one is an example of a nerd, as 'perhaps' warns.

blocks.note: first meaning: matters raised for discussion
second meaning: the four compass directions North, East, West, South

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals and the trailing dots make NEWS look like a headline about issues; it is the initials of the four cardinal directions on a compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Items for debate are points, and North, East, West and South are the cardinal compass bearings.

indicators.note: something dropped is let go and left out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the dish for cigarette ends
H is the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry has lost his cigarette accessory by letting it fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like the smoker's name, but it is the physics unit whose symbol is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has been lost or mislaid, which is exactly what missing means.

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who often has visitors over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receive guests' reads as one phrase about hosting; 'Receive' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a letter or gift is to be given it, a plain synonym of being handed something.

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An outrage: the saunas have gone cold and been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening word looks like a complaint about the saunas, but it is the definition, and 'destroyed' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandalous conduct shocks people and causes public outrage, just as offensive behaviour does.

clue.text: Edged in this way entering study backwards

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another
backwards means in the opposite direction, so the whole thing reads in reverse

blocks.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
'so' means in this way, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: Someone sidles into a study in reverse, edging in like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-letter word goes inside the room first, between its second and third letters, and only then is the whole five-letter string turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to move slowly and carefully, inching ahead, the same as edging along.

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is taken as it is heard rather than written

blocks.note: a spectacle is a sight

explanation.surface: Accountants are called in to witness some spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' looks like the people who check accounts; it is the older sense of hearers. In law, to cite someone is to call them to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite a person is to order them to appear before a court, a legal sense of summon.

clue.text: Strengths of a flipping politician one secures

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so its letters run the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
Lib is short for a Liberal
the Roman numeral for one
to secure a rope is to tie it

explanation.surface: The talents of a politician who keeps changing sides, as one secures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping politician' suggests a turncoat who flip-flops on policy; the flip simply turns the party abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: Your abilities are your skills and capacities, the things you are good at, so a plural noun synonym of strengths.

clue.text: Children nicked revolving piece for target

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the letters face the other way
to nick is to steal a small bit, so a short run of letters is lifted from the words around it

blocks.note: the last three letters of the first word and first two of the next

explanation.surface: Kids pinched a spinning part meant for an archery target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' looks like the children's crime, but it is lifting letters from 'Children nicked' itself, which are then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring of a target next to the bull's-eye, one of its scoring zones.

indicators.note: upset means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: six letters taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A nun is troubled by some German cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged sister goes round the single letter, which sits after her first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, one of the big cats, so the definition names the family it belongs to.

clue.text: Empty dairy next to foul house

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving just the outer shell of first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters
foul means nasty

explanation.surface: A deserted milk shed stands beside a filthy dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is not a building but a royal family line, as in the House of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a ruling family across generations, which is what a dynasty is.
